# Introduction 
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns 

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

```

The members of Insect Habitat Builders Club have been struggling with finding real estate for their insect terrariums for many years now. A new flower has started becoming more popular, and they want to see if the width of a flower petal is correlated to the length. Measurements of petals of flowers of different species were taken to test this, totalling `{python} f"{df.shape[0]}"` samples. 


# Literature Review 



# Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters), we will evaluate this relationship using a simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these. 




# Results 
```{python}
corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > 0.8: 
	narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0.4:
	narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
	narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -0.4:
	narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"


```

Using the classic simple Pearson correlation appraoch these data produce a correlation coefficient of `{python} f"{corr_val: .5f}"`, as such, given this result we conclude that the relationship is `{python} f"{narrative}"`.


```{python}

#| label: fig-length-width-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatterplot of petal length and width"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (6,3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')
 
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (mm)')


```

As shown in @fig-length-width-scatter, we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and petal width. 


# Discussion 

Now that this long-standing probelm is resolved thanks to the dilligent efforts of the Club, science has once again triumphed in establishing that there is a positive correlative relationship between Iris petal length and Iris petal width as a matter of empirically cetain round truth. 



```{python}
#| label: fig-length-width-lmplot
#| fig-cap: "A linear model plot of petal length and width"

sns.lmplot(data = df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')


```


```{python}

#| label: fig-length-width-hexplot
#| fig-cap: "A hexbin plot of petal length and width"

sns.jointplot(x = df['petal_length'], y = df['petal_width'], kind = 'hex', color = '#4CB391')


```
